newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks climb to new record highs.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks climb to new record highs.

text.p: Madrid stock indices climbed to new record highs on Wednesday and traders said they remained optimistic about the outlook in the medium term.
However traders said a bout of profit taking in late trade as Wall Street moved lower, could signal the start of a small correction in the short term.
The general index rose 6.05 points, 1.21 percent, to 504.41, while the Ibex-35 index climbed 72.23 points, 1.26 pct, to 5,802.26.
"Although we saw some selling this afternoon which could prompt a technical correction, the market is very strong and we are going to see yet more record highs," said one trader.
Turnover was high with more than 113 billion pesetas changing hands. Telefonica and Banco Popular were the most active stocks, attracting 27 percent of trade.
Banco Popular ended 2,100 pesetas, or 7.8 percent, higher at 29,050 after announcing it would buy back 35 billion pesetas' worth of its stock which would then be cancelled.
Popular also said it would split stock four for one, with the face value falling to 125 pesetas from 500 pesetas.
